article_manifest.title: Drug trafficking: two young people in their twenties arrested with 12,000 Tramadol tablets at the Tillabéri road barrier

article_manifest.summary: Published on Tuesday, December 30, 2025 | actuniger.com The vigilance of the security forces has once again borne fruit . On December 22, 2025, officers of the Yantala Police Station seized 12,000 Tramadol tablets during a routine check at the Tillabéri road barrier, thwarting an attempt to transport drugs to a gold site in the region, with the arrest of two young Nigeriens in their twenties .

article_manifest.title: Niger: Islamic State claims responsibility for attack on Niamey airport
article_manifest.original_title: Niger: l’Etat islamique revendique l’attaque de l’aéroport de Niamey
article_manifest.summary: Published on Friday, January 30, 2026 | AFP The Islamic State claimed responsibility on Friday for the attack on Niamey airport in Niger, said the Site group, which specializes in counter-terrorism research . On the night of Wednesday to Thursday, Niamey airport, which is home to military sites and is about ten kilometers from the presidency, was the target of an attack leaving 20 dead on the attacking side, according to the Nigerien military junta .

article_manifest.title: Niger Coup: Survival of the Military Regime and Growing Fragility
article_manifest.original_title: Niger Coup: Survival of the Military Regime and Growing Fragility
article_manifest.summary: The attempted coup in Niamey on the night of 28–29 August 2026 exposed a fundamental contradiction at the heart of General Abdourahamane Tiani’s rule. Although the regime survived its serious internal challenge since the July 2023 coup against Mohamed Bazoum, the episode revealed fractures within the armed forces, declining confidence in the government’s ability to improve security, and dependence on foreign military support.

article_manifest.title: Protection of asins, camels and horses in Burkina Faso: A new framework to better fight against trafficking
article_manifest.original_title: Protection des asins, camelins et équins au Burkina Faso : Un nouveau cadre pour mieux lutter contre le trafic
article_manifest.summary: The Directorate General of Veterinary Services (DGSV) organized, on October 2, 2026 in Ouagadougou, a workshop dedicated to the popularization of the new regulatory framework for asins, camels and horses . Administrative, religious and customary authorities, veterinary services, customs, defence and security forces, VDP and breeders' representatives took part in the meeting to take ownership of the new provisions and strengthen their application on the ground .

article_manifest.title: ARMY MUSEUM: the School of Application and Development of Officers to discover the military heritage of our country
article_manifest.original_title: MUSÉE DES ARMÉES : l’École d’Application et de Perfectionnement des Officiers à la découverte du patrimoine militaire de notre pays
article_manifest.summary: The Army Museum welcomed, this Friday, October 2, 2026, a delegation from the School of Application and Development of Officers (EAPO), as part of the educational activities of the institution. The purpose of this visit was to allow the trainees to learn more about the military history of Mali and to immerse themselves in the immense heritage bequeathed by previous generations of Malian combatants .

article_manifest.title: Tribute ceremony to Thomas Sankara: Minister Mathias Traoré invites the Burkinabe to preserve the legacy of the national hero
article_manifest.original_title: Cérémonial d’hommage à Thomas Sankara : Le ministre Mathias Traoré invite les Burkinabè à préserver l’héritage du héros national
article_manifest.summary: The authorities gathered at the foot of the statue of Thomas Sankara. The Thomas Sankara Memorial hosted, this Thursday, October 1, 2026 in Ouagadougou, the military ceremony in tribute to Captain Thomas Sankara and his twelve companions, who fell on October 15, 1987 The ceremony brought together several members of the government as well as representatives of international organizations, who came to pay tribute to the memory of the former president of Faso and to recall the scope of his legacy.

article_manifest.title: Celebration of the 66th anniversary of the Malian Army
article_manifest.original_title: Célébration du 66ᵉ anniversaire de l’Armée de Terre malienne
article_manifest.summary: On October 1, 2026, the Malian Army celebrated its 66th anniversary in Djicoroni-Para, under the theme: "The Army, 66 years in the service of the Nation: cohesion and resilience for the sovereign defense of Mali" . Composed in particular of the Infantry, the Artillery and the Armoured Weapon and Cavalry, the Army constitutes the main pillar of the land defence of the country.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso's military leaders mark four years in power
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso's military leaders mark four years in power
article_manifest.summary: People gathered in Ougadougou’s Place de la Révolution on Wednesday night to mark four years since Captain Ibrahim Traoré came to power in a coup. The culmination of anniversary celebrations, they paid tribute to the armed forces and the military government’s achievements in Burkina Faso. One resident, Abdoul Rasmané Sawadogo, said military leaders have created an “ultra-modern army that meets expectations”.

article_manifest.title: Mali: more than 2,400 schools remain closed as insecurity disrupts new school year
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: more than 2,400 schools remain closed as insecurity disrupts new school year
article_manifest.summary: Mali's new school year began Thursday with more than 2,400 schools unable to reopen, as worsening insecurity and the growing presence of jihadist groups continue to disrupt education. The 2026-2027 academic year has been declared the “Year of Education and Culture” by President Assimi Goïta, but thousands of children are starting the year without access to their classrooms.

article_manifest.title: Pix of the Day, 30 September, 2026 - Across the world
article_manifest.original_title: Pix of the Day, 30 September, 2026 - Across the world
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso has inaugurated its first gold refinery as its military-led government seeks to strengthen economic sovereignty after breaking ties with its traditional Western partners. “From now on, Burkina Faso’s gold must not only be mined in Burkina Faso; it must also be processed, controlled, valued and certified there,” President Ibrahim Traoré said on Monday at the inauguration of the refinery, named Raffinor-BF.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso opens first gold refinery in push for economic independence
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso opens first gold refinery in push for economic independence
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso opened its first gold refinery on Monday, pushing ahead with plans to better organise the commercialisation of the precious metal in one of the continent's top producers. The west African nation is the continent's third leading gold producer, churning out more than 94 tonnes of the precious metal last year, according to the World Gold Council. But authorities traditionally struggle to control the informal gold mining sector, which has been blighted by jihadist violence and smuggling.
